evidence: Vulg. Ps. 103 (104), 25: illīc rēptilia quōrum nōn est numerus
terms.comment: There, away from both of us: “over there”, of a place one can point to. It answers hīc, here.

evidence: Cic. Att. 4.1.4: ibi mihi Tulliola mea fuit praestō
Plaut. Asin. 117–117b: Nempe in forō? — Ibi.
terms.comment: The unemphatic “there”, pointing back to a place already named; it answers ubi. Also of time, “then” (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: ibi mihi Tulliola mea fuit praestō nātālī suō ipsō diē
phrases.english: there my little Tullia was waiting for me, on her very birthday

phrases.latin: in Tusculānum nōs ventūrōs putāmus aut Nōnīs aut postrīdiē. ibi ut sint omnia parāta
phrases.english: we expect to reach Tusculum on the Nones or the day after. See that everything is ready there

phrases.latin: Hoc mare magnum et spatiōsum manibus; illīc rēptilia quōrum nōn est numerus
phrases.english: this great sea, wide on every side: there are creeping things without number

phrases.latin: abscēde etiam nunc — etiam nunc — etiam — ohē, istīc astātō.
phrases.english: Move back a bit more — more — more — whoa, stand there.

phrases.latin: vōs, meae cārissimae animae, quam saepissimē ad mē scrībite et vōs quid agātis et quid istīc agātur
phrases.english: my dearest souls, write to me as often as you can, both how you are and what is going on there
